questions.question: In the experimental simulation, thickness measurements were recorded at four points: T₁ = 2.57 mm, T₂ = 2.45 mm, T₃ = 2.51 mm, and T₄ = 2.48 mm. What is the arithmetic mean thickness (T_avg) of the leather specimen?
The digital Vernier caliper recorded orthogonal diameters of d₁ = 68.98 mm and d₂ = 70.02 mm. What are the resulting mean diameter (d) and cross-sectional surface area (A)?
Given specimen mass m = 6.751 g, mean thickness T_avg = 2.502 mm, and mean diameter d = 69.50 mm, what is the apparent density (ρ) calculated via ISO 2420: ρ = (1.273 × 10⁶ × m) / (T_avg × d²)?
What is the total apparent (envelope) volume (V) of the test specimen in the simulation, and how does it relate mass (m = 6.751 g) to density in CGS units?
Based on the measured mass m = 6.751 g and cross-sectional area A = 37.94 cm², what is the mass per unit area (substance / grammage, q_A) of this leather in g/m²?
Assuming a true solid matrix collagen density of ρ_t = 1.38 g/cm³, what is the calculated void fraction (internal porosity, ε) of the tested specimen (apparent density ρ = 0.7114 g/cm³)?
An apparent density of 711.425 kg/m³ (0.711 g/cm³) with a mean thickness of 2.502 mm indicates that the tested material conforms to which industrial leather category?

answers.a: Vegetable-tanned heavy sole leather (density typically > 0.95 g/cm³)
answers.b: Chrome-tanned bovine shoe upper / boot leather (density typically 0.68 to 0.78 g/cm³)
answers.c: Ultra-light lambskin garment nappa (density typically 0.45 to 0.55 g/cm³)
answers.d: Compressed bonded leather fibre board (density typically > 1.10 g/cm³)

questions.question: If a dull cutting die is used, causing severe beveling where the bottom face diameter is smaller than the top face, what systematic error occurs in the calculated apparent density?

answers.a: Apparent density will be artificially overestimated because the true specimen volume is smaller than the cylinder volume computed from top diameter
answers.b: Apparent density will be underestimated because mass increases proportionally
answers.c: Apparent density remains completely unaffected as geometric shape has no influence on density
answers.d: The thickness gauge reading will drop to exactly 0.00 mm

questions.question: Why must the dead-weight thickness measurement reading be taken exactly 5 ± 1 seconds after the presser foot contacts the leather specimen?

answers.a: To allow the optical digital encoder to recharge its battery
answers.b: To capture the initial elastic response while avoiding substantial long-term viscoelastic creep, thereby ensuring reproducible thickness data across laboratories
answers.c: To allow frictional heat generated by the foot landing to dissipate completely
answers.d: To ensure moisture in the specimen is driven out into the surrounding air

questions.question: How would testing a leather specimen in a completely unconditioned, bone-dry state (0% moisture content) distort the apparent density compared to standard ISO 2419 conditioned testing (65% RH)?

answers.a: Both mass and volume would increase equally, keeping density exactly constant
answers.b: The bone-dry specimen would have lower mass due to moisture loss and lower volume due to fibril shrinkage, with apparent density shifting unpredictably depending on the shrinkage-to-mass-loss ratio
answers.c: Density would always triple because moisture repels collagen molecules
answers.d: The specimen would chemically decompose and cannot be weighed
